title: Epic Recruiting Hackathon
description:
The Epic AI Recruiting Hackathon lets employers observe candidates solving a real business challenge with AI before deciding whom to interview.

It reveals how candidates frame problems, collaborate, prompt and challenge AI, verify information, apply human judgement and turn ambiguity into credible solutions.

AI dexterity must be seen in action. Asking candidates how they use AI produces a description. Watching them use it produces evidence.

The hackathon also makes interviews more valuable, allowing recruiters to explore decisions and behaviours they have already observed.

Don’t ask talent what it can do. Watch it happen.

title: Hire Your AI Team in Minutes
description:
What Can AI Workers Do for Your Business? 

Could an AI Worker save your team time, take repetitive work off their plate and help your business move faster?

AI has evolved quickly—from LLMs and chatbots to copilots, agents and AI Workers. But these concepts are often used interchangeably, making it difficult for businesses to understand what each can actually do and where the real value lies.

In this practical workshop, we’ll cut through the hype and explore how different types of AI can support people, teams and real business workflows.

Together, we’ll explore: • The differences between LLMs, chatbots, copilots, AI agents and AI Workers 

• When each type of AI is most useful, and why they are not interchangeable

• What allows an AI Worker to support ongoing work, rather than simply respond to individual prompts

• Real tasks and workflows AI Workers can take on across operations, customer support, sales, marketing, research and analysis

• How to identify where an AI Worker could save time, reduce repetitive work or help a team operate more effectively.

 After exploring the concepts and real business use cases, participants will put what they’ve learned into practice by hiring their first AI Worker through Spinnable and identifying a workflow it could support. 

By the end of the session, they’ll leave not only with a clearer understanding of AI Workers, but with a concrete first step towards using one in their business.

No coding or technical background is required. The session is designed for founders, startups, SMBs, business teams and anyone curious about applying AI to real work.

Speakers: Vasco Pedro (Co-founder & CEO of Spinnable) Gil Coelho (Co-founder & CPO of Spinnable) 📅 Thursday, 24 September 2026 ⏰ 6:00pm 📍 Avila Spaces Saldanha, Lisbon

title: How to Sell Authentically in the Age of AI, while still using AI
description:
This is a hands-on session for entrepreneurs and founders who want to stand out, sell more, and sound like themselves, while still using AI.  

Here's the truth about where we are right now: With AI, we can produce competent marketing in seconds. The clever hook, the optimized page, the whole nurture sequence. And everyone has the same tools, pointed at the same playbook, making the same content. So the thing that used to set you apart, sounding polished, is now the cheapest thing in the room.

Which means It's not who sounds the most impressive anymore. It's who feels the most real, relatable, and trustworthy.  That's the one thing a machine can't copy, and it's the thing most business owners lose access to at the exact moment it counts.

In this workshop session, I'll show your group how to get it back, and we’ll make it practical. We'll cover:

A copy-paste prompt you can use that night to draft a landing page, and the one thing you have to feed it that AI can't come up with on its own.

The core parts every sales page that sells actually needs, in a simple framework you'll use again and again.

A live rewrite, where we take a flat, AI-generic copy and turn it into something that sounds like a real human, in real time. You'll feel the difference the moment it happens.

Everyone leaves with the prompt, the framework, and a new way of seeing their own words.

title: Reverse-Engineering the AI Answer
description: AI assistants like ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity are already answering questions about brands, products and competitors, and most companies have no idea what they say. Unlike a search results page, these answers are generated on the fly, change from one query to the next, and rarely show their sources. Measuring them means treating AI answers as data: asking the same questions at scale, extracting which brands get mentioned and cited, and tracking how that changes over time. This session shows how that works in practice, what the data reveals about how brands actually appear in AI answers, and what marketing, SEO and product teams can do about it.

title: AI OS: como operar IA com um sistema, não com truques — sessão ao vivo com Inês Lourenço
description:
Concept. "Using AI" and "operating AI" are different things, and the difference is having a system. Most tech professionals restart from zero every time they open a chat: they re-explain who they are, what they do, how they want the answer — and get back text that is competent and generic. The AI OS is the alternative: a small operating system for working with AI that you build once and maintain in thirty minutes a week.

In 60 minutes, in Portuguese and on a shared screen, Inês Lourenço walks through the five layers with her own real setup: Context (what your AI knows about you — the cheapest layer to build and the one that pays most per hour invested), Connections (which tools it can reach, and with what declared purpose), Skills (work patterns saved as reusable files, with the rule of the third time), Automations (prompts with a schedule and a size limit) and Memory (approved, typed, portable — never "save everything"). Then the loop that keeps it alive: the Weekly Audit, thirty minutes every Friday in which the system proposes and you approve, reject or delete. The session closes with live Q&A built from the questions submitted at registration.

Who is speaking. Inês Lourenço is Chief Product Officer at Leadfeeder and was VP of Product Growth at Usercentrics, where she helped scale the company to €100M ARR. Fifteen years operating B2B SaaS teams across Lisbon, Helsinki and Berlin; keynote speaker at SaaSiest and Craftmatters 2026. She teaches what she runs every day.

Objectives. Give participants a method they can apply the next morning, not a tour of tools. Every participant leaves with (1) a 0–20 diagnostic of their own AI system, layer by layer, (2) the first automation drafted in three lines, and (3) free access to the five-module AIOS for Tech Professionals mini-course, with a final test and a verifiable certificate.

description:

Legal and professional services are full of complex, high-value problems that remain underserved by technology. PAXFORGE is designed to turn some of those problems into opportunities for building practical, scalable and commercially relevant products.

During the hackathon, participants will be presented with a specific challenge drawn from the needs of legal and professional services organisations. Working individually or in teams, they will have one day to develop a working prototype using whatever technologies and approaches they consider most effective.

Challenges may involve areas such as document processing, entity and relationship mapping, risk assessment, alerts, workflow automation, data governance, knowledge management and CRM integrations.

The objective is to move beyond ideas and build something that could realistically be used in practice.

Following the hackathon, selected teams will have the opportunity to validate their solutions with Paxrocket, Paxlegal and relevant industry professionals. This may include product feedback, testing against real-world requirements, legal and operational guidance, and support in identifying potential users and use cases.

The strongest projects may then have the opportunity to continue developing with Paxrocket and Paxlegal, creating a pathway towards further validation, pilot projects, potential adoption and commercialisation.

title: The role of AI in banking and financial crime prevention
description:
Financial crime is evolving faster than ever, growing more sophisticated, automated, and harder to detect using traditional rule-based systems. In response, banks worldwide are turning to artificial intelligence not merely as a defensive tool, but as a strategic capability that reshapes how they operate, compete, and build trust with customers. Portugal has quietly become a meaningful hub in this transformation, home to Feedzai, a global leader in AI-powered risk management, and to banks that are among the most advanced adopters of AI for fraud and financial crime prevention anywhere in Europe.

This panel brings together two of Portugal's leading banks — Caixa Geral de Depósitos and Novobanco — to share how they have integrated AI into their financial crime prevention strategies, and what they've learned along the way. Manuel Fonseca Soares at Caixa Geral de Depósitos, and João Morais Fernandes of Novobanco, will discuss the practical realities of deploying AI at scale: balancing detection accuracy with operational efficiency, navigating regulatory expectations, and managing the trust implications of automated decision-making in a highly sensitive domain. The conversation will be moderated by a member of Feedzai's Research team, bringing a research-driven perspective to ground the discussion in both the current state of the art and the trajectory of where AI-driven financial crime prevention is heading.

Objectives

The panel aims to move beyond high-level narratives about "AI in banking" and offer a grounded, first-hand account of what it actually takes to adopt AI for financial crime prevention at two major institutions: the organizational, technical, and cultural challenges involved, and the measurable impact on both risk reduction and business operations. It is designed for a mixed audience of technical and business attendees at Lisbon AI Week, offering value whether someone is building AI systems, deploying them, or governing their use.

title: Cafe Compute Meetup: Lisbon
description:
Cafe Compute is Cerebras' global community meetup format - a relaxed, hands-on evening where people build rather than just listen. Cerebras and OpenAI are bringing it to Lisbon for Lisbon AI Week, hosted by Cerebras Community Ambassador Francisco Ribeiro.

The evening runs on a tight two-hour arc. Doors open with drinks and pizza. A 15-minute introduction covers Cerebras, the Wafer-Scale Engine (WSE-3, the world's largest AI chip) and why inference speed changes what you can realistically build. The bulk of the time is a live coding session: attendees work on their own laptops against Cerebras Inference and OpenAI Codex-Spark, plus open-source models such as GLM 4.7, with the hosts on hand to unblock people. The evening closes with open networking.

OBJECTIVES

1. Give Lisbon's developer community direct, practical exposure to frontier inference hardware - up to 15x faster than leading GPUs - instead of a slide deck about it.

2. Lower the barrier to actually trying it: every attendee leaves with a Cerebras API key and free compute credits, so what starts in the room can continue afterwards.

3. Connect the people building with AI in Lisbon - independent developers, startup engineering teams and enterprise technologists - in a setting where conversation happens naturally rather than through a Q&A microphone.

EXPECTED IMPACT

We expect 60-80 people in the room. The measurable outcome is working code: prototypes and experiments started on the night and continued afterwards on free credits. The softer outcome matters as much - Lisbon gains a recurring, low-friction technical meetup with a global sponsor behind it, and Lisbon AI Week gains a genuinely hands-on entry in the programme to balance the talks and panels. Cafe Compute runs in cities worldwide; a strong Lisbon edition makes this a repeating fixture rather than a one-off, and strengthens the Iberian ambassador cluster already forming between Lisbon, Madrid and Barcelona.

The event is free to attend, held in Englis

title: AI Night Thinkers - Live edition
description:
Concept. Most AI events in Portugal are built around speakers describing what is possible. AI Night Thinkers is built around people showing what they have made. The format is deliberately unpolished: four members of our community each get 15 minutes, a shared screen and a working project. Questions from the room follow immediately, and they tend to be technical and direct. What gets demonstrated ranges from small automations solving a genuine personal problem to early-stage products with paying users.

We have run this format twice monthly since the Hub began, online. For Lisbon AI Week we are staging it in person for the first time, in Cascais, with a live stream so the wider community can join remotely. The session is recorded and archived.

Objectives. First, to show a side of the Portuguese AI scene that conferences rarely surface — the practitioners who are quietly building rather than speaking. Second, to give our community a stage during the most visible AI week of the year. Third, to connect builders based in the Cascais area with visitors who came to Lisbon for the week and would not otherwise cross paths with them.

Why Cascais. There is a substantial technical and entrepreneurial population in the Cascais area — founders, freelancers, engineers, a large international community — that does not travel into Lisbon midweek for an evening event. Our proposition is not to move audience out of the city, but to activate an audience that already exists thirty minutes down the line and rarely appears in the capital's programming. Cascais is ten minutes by train from Cais do Sodré every ten minutes, so the event remains fully accessible to anyone attending the week.

Expected impact. Between 40 and 50 attendees in the room, plus the live stream audience. A recorded archive that remains publicly available afterwards. The concept combines AI film screenings, an AI tool demonstration, an AI artist talk and informal networking in an outdoor setting, creating a space where the community can not only discover new AI technologies and creative work, but also exchange ideas and experiences around how these tools are being used in real creative workflows.

The main objectives are to:

→ Showcase emerging AI filmmaking and creative work, giving creators a platform to present their films to a live audience.

→ Share practical knowledge about AI tools, through live demonstrations and real examples of their application in visual media.

→ Connect the creative community, bringing together artists, filmmakers, agencies, brands and creative technologists for meaningful in-person exchange.

→ Encourage experimentation and collaboration between people working across AI, film, art and advertising.

→ Strengthen Lisbon’s creative AI ecosystem by creating an accessible space for international and local creators to meet and share knowledge.

The expected impact is to increase visibility for AI creators and emerging creative technologies, facilitate new connections and collaborations, and contribute to a stronger, more connected community around AI and the creative industries in Lisbon.

The event is also designed to make AI feel practical, accessible and community-driven — moving beyond discussion about the technology and focusing on the people, creative work and workflows being developed with it.

title: Eleven Yellow Sessions #01 - AI x GTM
description:
Eleven Yellow Sessions is a new recurring format we're launching, and Lisbon AI Week felt like the right place to kick it off. This first edition is themed around AI and Growth/GTM.

Concept: Rather than a panel or a set of formal presentations, this is a workflow-sharing session. Each speaker walks the room through something concrete they actually do — a tool, an automation, a process — and opens it up for questions as they go. Nobody is presenting a deck or pitching a product; the format is closer to "let me show you what's on my screen" than a keynote.

Confirmed speakers so far:

- Selo (José Sáez), CEO of Eleven Yellow, on using Nodo (Eleven Yellow's internal AI automation tool) to automate GTM workflows.

- The Head of Growth at Gravl, the world's largest personal training app, on running large-scale performance marketing with AI.

- A specialist on building automated, AI-driven email marketing campaigns.

- A founder from a Lisbon-based AI influencer marketing studio, sharing their own workflows in that space.

Format: roughly one hour of short workflow walkthroughs (15–20 min each) with live Q&A, followed by an hour of drinks and informal networking, hosted at Eleven Yellow's own office. The session is intentionally small and curated (request-to-join) rather than an open broadcast, to keep the room practitioner-heavy and the conversation useful rather than performative.

Objectives: 

1) Give growth professionals real, applicable AI workflows they can take home — not inspiration, but tactics.

2) Create a low-key, non-commercial space where people share what they're actually building, rather than what they're selling.

Expected impact: attendees leave with concrete workflows and tools they can implement immediately, plus direct access to practitioners running serious AI-driven growth operations. For Eleven Yellow, it's an opportunity to build community around a recurring event format.

title: Cascais AI Afterwork
description:
Concept. By Friday evening of a week like this, most people have absorbed as much programmed content as they can usefully take in. What tends to be in short supply is unstructured time with the people they have been sitting next to.

The Cascais AI Afterwork is designed around that observation. There is no stage, no agenda and nobody presenting. It is drinks and conversation at sunset, on the coast, hosted by a community that has been meeting in Cascais twice a month since the Hub began.

Objectives. To give attendees of Lisbon AI Week a genuinely different way to close the week, and to connect the Cascais AI community with visitors who have come to Lisbon for it. In our experience running community gatherings, the conversations that lead to actual collaboration rarely happen in the session — they happen afterwards, and they happen better when nobody is trying to run anything.

Why Cascais, and why Friday. The setting is the point. Cascais is thirty minutes from Cais do Sodré, with trains every ten minutes running late into the evening, so it is fully accessible to anyone in the city. Placing it on Friday evening means it competes with nothing in the programme and functions as a natural closing point for the week — the trip out of the city becomes part of the experience rather than an obstacle.

It also brings visitors into contact with a local community they are unlikely to encounter otherwise: founders, engineers, freelancers and a substantial international population based in the Cascais area who do not routinely attend evening events in Lisbon.

Expected impact. Between 70 and 80 attendees, mixing our existing community with visitors from the week. We expect this to be the most accessible event in our cluster and the one that generates the most connections per hour. Venue on the waterfront, capacity managed through advance registration.

title: Build Your Product with AI: 4-Hour Intensive Workshop (Barreiro Edition)
description:
Concept: a 4-hour live build session where participants stop talking about their app idea and actually build it. The workshop takes non-technical entrepreneurs from concept to working prototype using AI-powered development tools (Lovable, Supabase and vibe coding). It is deliberately not a demo where people watch someone else build: every participant leaves with their own working product.

How the 4 hours work. Phase 1, Foundation: software architecture for non-tech entrepreneurs, simplified. We vote a business idea together, turn it into a Product Requirements Document and build it live, while digging into the tools used in the workshop. Phase 2, Build Time (2.5 hours): participants form small teams (or work alone) around complementary ideas and build hands-on with AI tools, with direct support and real-time problem solving. Phase 3, Showcase (30 minutes): each team presents their working product, gets feedback and next steps.

Objectives: make AI-powered product development accessible to founders, business owners and creators with no technical background; give them a repeatable workflow and templates (PRD template, prompts, guides) they can reuse after the event; and create a space where local entrepreneurs meet and pitch ideas to each other.

Expected impact: this is the first edition of the workshop in Margem Sul, hosted at Startup Barreiro, the municipal business incubator of Barreiro, in partnership with the Municipio do Barreiro. It brings Lisbon AI Week across the river, connecting the Lisbon AI and founder communities (Lx Entrepreneurs and Creators, 949 members, and VibeFounders Lisbon, 608 members) with the growing entrepreneurial ecosystem of the south bank. Previous editions in Lisbon (LACS, Kube) sold out.

Instructor: Alex Russo, founder of WebYourMind and community owner of Lx Entrepreneurs and Creators and VibeFounders Lisbon, 20+ years in tech including Fortune 100 product work, 20,000+ students taught online.

Practical: 25 seats, 65 EUR per ticket

title: CryptoFriday x Lisbon AI week - AI Agents: Can We Trust Them?
description:
CryptoFriday is The Block Lisboa's flagship weekly event, running every Friday since 2017, with a community of 6,500+ members. For Lisbon AI Week, we're theming it around one of the most pressing questions in tech right now: how far can we trust autonomous AI agents?

AI agents are multiplying fast and starting to execute real-world actions — trading, payments, financial and security decisions. But they remain hard to audit and predict. AI is scaling faster than the trust we can reasonably place in it, and that gap is the conversation.

The evening opens with a short, informal talk led by Tyler M (EZ Labs / VeriMesh). It includes a live demo of a trading agent's logic under deterministic guardrails, and an audience challenge: participants propose an agent action and see how the system would verify or reject it in real time. From there we open the floor with questions designed to get everyone talking — would you trust an AI agent to trade your money? If you ran a fund, what would you require an agent to prove before it moved a million?

The talk is followed by open networking. CryptoFriday's role during AI Week is to be the social anchor of the week — the place where people who spent their days in workshops, hackathons, and talks finally meet one another and turn ideas into collaborations.

Free and open to everyone. Held in English, given the international profile of our community.

title: HABITAR — What Artificial Intelligence Forces Us to Rediscover About Being Human
description:
Artificial intelligence is rapidly expanding what can be generated, predicted, analysed, automated and delegated.

Most conversations about AI understandably focus on what machines will soon be capable of doing.

HABITAR begins somewhere else.  It asks what the emergence of increasingly capable artificial intelligence reveals about us. 

When machines can write, compose, calculate, analyse, remember and create alongside us, many of the capacities we once considered unquestionably human can no longer be taken for granted.

And perhaps that gives us an unexpected opportunity: to look more carefully at the experience of being human itself.

HABITAR — What Artificial Intelligence Forces Us to Rediscover About Being Human is an intimate experiential workshop situated at the intersection of psychology, neuroscience, human experience and contemporary culture. 

Rather than offering another prediction about the future of artificial intelligence, the session creates a space in which participants can explore what may become increasingly important precisely because so much else can be outsourced.

Attention.  Embodiment.  Memory.  Relationship.  Sensory experience.  Creativity.  Meaning.  Presence.  

The experience moves between conceptual exploration, conversation and hands-on analogue practices using simple materials such as paper, images, thread and collage.

Participants are invited not simply to think about humanity, but to experience these questions through their own hands, memories, perceptions and ways of making meaning.

Throughout the workshop, one question remains present:

What does it mean to inhabit a human life in an age of increasing artificial intelligence?  

The session concludes with the creation of a small personal artefact and a collective piece bringing together traces, words, materials and reflections from the people in the room.

HABITAR proposes that one of the most important conversations about artificial intelligence may ultimately be a conversation about humanity.

About what we choose to pay attention to.

What we continue to make with our own hands.

What we remember.

How we relate to one another.

 And, ultimately, how we choose to inhabit our lives.

title: Build Your AI System
description:
AI's default interface is a chat box. That's a demo, not a system. The model is stateless, so you re-explain everything, and judgement stays with you while the tool forgets. The result is impressive one-offs and no compounding leverage.

This is a working session. You leave with an AI system installed and understood — not a slide deck.

Objectives: replace "prompting" as the mental model; install a working system on your machine; understand each layer well enough to extend it; ship one automation the same day.

Impact: participants stop treating AI as a novelty tab and start running real work through a system they own.

Practical details: full day, 10:00–17:00; English; cap 16; €397 per person; laptop required. Hosted by André Casal (Casal Innovations, Lda).
